title: Fourier component on a coordinate set
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ has one basis vector equal to the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For a function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and a set $S$ of coordinates, its orthogonal component at $S$ is the Fourier component of $f$ supported on $S$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nonempty basis index set $\iota$
A basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ with a constant-one basis vector
Orthonormality of the basis for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
caveat: The referenced definition of the Fourier component at a support is omitted, so its construction cannot be stated precisely from the supplied snippet.
